findings.issue: Production refresh dates are reconstructed from positive-gross box-office history. A degraded pre-season refresh with zero resolved grosses persists neither box-office nor forecast rows, so its date disappears from later history charts and the line connects across the missing observation instead of preserving the required gap.
findings.suggestion: Persist every production refresh date independently of gross and forecast rows, and use that durable record when constructing the history axis.

findings.issue: For an aliased chart title, the variant override always wins the `or` lookup even when it contains only `alias_of`. Consequently, a release-date correction stored on the canonical title is ignored, so a valid alias-plus-canonical-correction configuration can filter out the film or infer the wrong status.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the variant and canonical overrides separately, using variant metadata when present and otherwise falling back to the canonical override's release_date.

findings.issue: Box-office history rows are not schema-validated at the load boundary. Values such as a negative cumulative gross or non-string movie title can be accepted and silently produce missing or incorrect projections, contrary to the requirement that malformed persisted data fail during loading.
findings.suggestion: Validate each row as a mapping with a non-empty string movie, ISO date, and finite non-negative numeric cumulative_gross before adding it to history.

findings.issue: Direct-label collision handling only moves labels downward and does not constrain them to the SVG bounds. Several players with equal or low odds can therefore have labels clipped below the viewBox.
findings.suggestion: Use a bounded label-layout pass that maintains the minimum gap while keeping every label inside the plot bounds.
